newsitem.title: UK: UK business more upbeat than rest of Europe - poll.
newsitem.headline: UK business more upbeat than rest of Europe - poll.

text.p: Business confidence about growth prospects and the domestic economy is higher in Britain than anywhere else in Europe, according to the European Enterprise Index, published by the 3i European Enterprise centre.
A survey released on Tuesday showed France has replaced Germany as the country with the lowest levels of confidence amongst independent entrepreneurs.
The poll is conducted every six months amongst 8,000 small and medium sized enterprises in Britain, France, Germany, Italy and Spain. It was carried out in July.

The centre's main Enterprise Index comprises the Economy and Business Indices which reflect expectations about the commercial environment and competition, and performance, expenditure and investment in companies respectively.
Firms in Britain and Spain are the most optimistic about investment in property, plant and equipment, and information technology over the next six months, the poll showed.

The two countries are the only ones showing a marked increase in optimism about the commercial environment and expecting improved performance levels measured in terms of labour, profitability and turnover.

In Britain, 27 percent of small and medium sized companies surveyed expect to raise additional finance in the next six months, slightly up from the previous rating of 25 percent. Increased expenditure is expected in marketing, research and development and training. The survey indicated that 3i's Competition Index remained negative throughout Europe, with French business people the least confident and a slight fall in Italy, where small businesses are worried about the country's economic situation.
Italy was the only one of the five countries to witness a downturn in expectations for the commercial environment.
France's ratings fell in all the main areas associated with business environment, as did Germany's, except for performance, which remained stable from the last survey six months before.
French companies polled expect to shed labour and experience declining profitability, with low levels of investment seen except in the areas of plant and equipment and information technology.
German small companies anticipate spending less on training, marketing and research and development but see investment in information technology improving.

There was also a sharp jump in in Germany among those expecting to raise additional finance, to 46 percent of those polled from 19 percent last time. Only eight percent expect gearing to increase, down from 20 percent previously.
